.name

Restrictions

Generic top-level domain. Introduced in 2001, although it did not become operational until January 2002. It is currently managed by the Global Name Registry. This domain was created specifically for individuals—real or fictional—and was originally intended to follow the structure first.last.name, but today the registered domain format is unrestricted.

.cz

Restrictions

National top-level domain (ccTLD) assigned to the Czech Republic. The domain name must contain 3 to 63 characters excluding the TLD. It can be registered by both companies and private individuals. Accepted characters: ‘a-z’, ‘0-9’, “-” (not as the first or last character). Annual registration duration. No specific restrictions.
